title: Process late-arriving usage and rate-limit credits in billing export pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing recurring invoice mismatches and NetSuite export rejections caused by late-arriving usage events and post-hoc rate-limit credits. These edge cases create negative invoice line items, duplicate external IDs in NetSuite, and Stripe proration drift when usage is applied after an invoice has already been closed. Root cause: ingestion pipeline accepts out-of-order events (LATE_USAGE) which currently get merged into the same hourly aggregation without a distinct export treatment. When a rate-limit credit is issued later (credit events), the existing export job mutates prior invoice lines instead of emitting an idempotent adjustment record. NetSuite rejects some exports because the external_id (export_id) collides; Stripe proration calculations are inconsistent because the billing export does not attach the original invoice reference or proration metadata.
tasks: Add a dedicated 'late_usage_adjustments' export channel that creates idempotent adjustment records with external_id = original_invoice_id + '-adj-' + adjustment_uuid
Change hourly rollup job to tag events with 'arrival_window' and route late events (arrival > 2 hours after event_timestamp) to adjustment channel
Compute deterministic proration_offset for any adjustment and attach 'proration_basis_invoice' field to Stripe line metadata
Update NetSuite mapping to include adjustment external_id and allow negative-line synchronization; add de-duplication based on (customer_id, external_id)
Backfill job: reprocess last 30 days of late events, emit adjustments, and create net new credit invoices where appropriate
Add e2e integration tests covering idempotent retries and duplicate-export rejection scenarios
Dashboard: add a 'late-usage adjustments' dashboard and alert when >0.25% of daily tokens are adjusted
Run a canary: enable adjustment channel for 10% of tenants for two days, validate invoice parity vs baseline
acceptance_criteria: All late-arriving usage and rate-limit credits are exported using idempotent adjustment records (no mutation of historical invoice lines)
NetSuite no longer rejects exports due to duplicate external_id; dedupe logic handles retry/duplicate cases
Stripe invoices reflect proration offsets via attached metadata and resulting invoice totals match Redwood accounting within 0.2% for canary tenants
Backfill completes for last 30 days without creating unapplied duplicates; backfilled adjustments include audit metadata and links to originating events
Monitoring in place: daily discrepancy metric, alerting when adjustments exceed threshold, and an automated reconciliation report available to finance
